Shaped iteration 0195 (#837). Iteration 0194 made no progress: author #834 was blocked because its file tools returned "disabled for this session". It saved nothing and read no files (`.session/reports/834.json`; record `.session/history/records/0194.json`). Review #835 never ran because it was blocked by the author task.

Graph (`.session/tasks.json`, passes the direct Python JSON, field and heading check with exit 0):
- `positive-control-author-0195` (benchmark, default model, medium effort, 60 min / 45 turns): the same step 4 work as #834. It adds wrong-literal and wrong-citation mutation controls for A0001 and A0002 to the score.py self-test, answers F4 from the inventory citation dicts, regenerates `benchmark/results/challenges.json` and updates all pins. The new first acceptance item is a tool probe (one Read, one Grep): if the tools are disabled, the session reports the exact error and stops. The #828, #831 and #834 reports are explicitly exported. Nothing from #834 can be resumed because it saved nothing.
- `positive-control-review-0195` (reviewer, default model, medium effort, 40 min / 30 turns), `blocked_by` the author task: it writes pins first, runs the self-test on a temporary copy and returns CLEAR or NOT-CLEAR.

I re-ordered the work rather than dropping it because the failure came from the environment, not from the task. Tools were disabled mid-session three times in a row (#828, #831, #834), so I sent the Policymaker an evidenced suggestion in `.session/suggestions.json`.

## What next
- Check the author's tool-probe line and the review verdict. CLEAR closes the positive-control thread; NOT-CLEAR means correcting only the named findings.
- If 0195 is blocked the same way, do not order this task a third time. Order a single measurement task (tool probe plus report) or wait for the Policymaker to act (`journal/working-memory.md` State).
